notes: What is measured and what is not. The inventory is derived from the four permitted checked-in sources; every entry carries a citation whose quotation the checker re-finds in the cited section, so nothing here is recalled. Much of what the contract asks about the legacy system is not reachable from this repository, and that part is enumerated as 9 gaps rather than filled in: 2 of 21 command ids and 38 of 47 modules are counted by the source but not named; 17 of 220 tests and 1 of 32 test files are not attributed to an area; the durable tables' column names are not in any permitted source; the two build scripts are not individually named; the four provider dialects' wire event vocabularies are not enumerated; no sanitized fixture corpus exists; and the configuration surface is deferred to the identifier inventory, which owns it. Two of the gaps are discrepancies inside the source itself, found by reconciling its stated counts against its own enumerations: it states 21 commands and lists 19, and it states 38 dashboard routes and lists 39. Both are reported, neither is silently reconciled. 12 entries have no owner because the porting map does not determine one; three of those are safety rows, and they are findings for the parity-ledger item, not defects hidden here. Granularity is recorded per entry: 38 parity-ledger rows are capability-level and 157 enumerated surfaces are surface-level, and they overlap by design, so per-family counts are published beside the per-class ones rather than presenting 195 as 195 distinct behaviours. What the checker cannot see, stated plainly: it refuses an invented owner, an uncited entry, a class outside the seven, an incomplete or self-contradicting fixture plan, a stale or hand-edited artifact and a count the source no longer supports, but it cannot tell a defensible class assignment from a wrong one. The classification judgements live in tools/contract_inventory/rules.toml, one row per family or parity row, so a reviewer can read all of them in one file rather than hunting them through 195 generated entries. The drift check is a self-contained module with its own main(); wiring it into plan/check.py is the follow-up for the integrator, deliberately not done here because several items share that file. This inventory is evidence for the sanitized fixture corpus and machine-readable parity ledger items and satisfies neither; it captures no fixture and closes no gate. No subagent was launched: the work is one generator, one checker and their tests, on a single lease.
